name: Index Put Portfolio Hedge
summary: Hedge a basket of correlated share positions with beta-weighted SPY or QQQ puts instead of hedging each name individually.

legs.strike_rule: SPY/QQQ put at 0.25-0.35 delta; contracts = (portfolio_value x portfolio_beta) / (index_price x 100 x hedge_ratio)

max_profit: grows as the index falls; offsets book losses to the extent beta holds
max_loss: premium paid, plus basis risk if the book falls while the index does not
breakevens: index level = strike - premium per share

greeks.delta: negative index delta sized to offset a chosen fraction of the book's beta-weighted delta

when_to_use: When the share book has 4+ correlated positions and hedging each individually is too expensive or illiquid. Especially good for a TickAverager-style multi-ticker fleet that is structurally long many correlated names.
entry_rules: Compute portfolio beta to SPY over the trailing 60 trading days; require R-squared >= 0.60 or the hedge has too much basis risk.
contracts = round((portfolio_value x beta x hedge_ratio) / (SPY_price x 100)), hedge_ratio default 0.5 (half hedge).
Require IV Rank on the index <= 45.
Premium budget <= 1.5% of portfolio value per 60-day hedge.
management_rules: Rebalance the contract count whenever portfolio value or beta drifts by more than 20% from the hedge sizing.
Monetize at 3x premium: sell half and re-strike.

Reduce hedge_ratio to 0.25 when the index is more than 10% below its 200-day SMA (the hedge is expensive and the damage is done); raise toward 0.75 when the index is above its 200-day SMA and VIX < 15.
exit_rules: Close ITM index puts before expiration - SPY/QQQ are share-settled ETFs and auto-exercise creates a SHORT ETF position of 100 shares per contract, which the account does not hold.
Remove the hedge when the underlying share book is reduced below the hedge's notional.
Hard close by 15:30 ET on expiration day.
assignment_risk: No short leg. Critical nuance: SPY, QQQ and IWM options are AMERICAN and settle in SHARES, unlike SPX/XSP which are European and cash-settled. An ITM long ETF put that auto-exercises delivers short ETF shares. If the system ever wants true cash settlement it must use index options (SPX/XSP/NDX), which are a different product and a different approval path.
liquidity_needs: SPY/QQQ - the most liquid options in the world; no constraint.
common_mistakes: Ignoring basis risk (hedging small caps with SPY); over-hedging so the book cannot make money in a rally; forgetting ETF options are physically settled.
zero_dte_notes: 0DTE index puts hedge only the current session and are better replaced by reducing share exposure directly.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
